no: Let ABC be a triangle, P a point and A'B'C' the circumcevian triangle of P. Let A_{b}, A_{c} be the orthogonal projections of P in A'C and A'B, respectively, and build B_{c}, B_{a} and C_{a}, C_{b} cyclically. Let A"B"C" be the triangle bounded by the lines A_{b}A_{c}, B_{c}B_{a} and C_{a}C_{b}. Then A"B"C" and ABC are perspective. (Abdilkadir Altintas, `problem 1540 <https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ngkMEaUueL4600mI7W_tK-90hJs8F6Hy/view>`__). If P= \(x:y:z\) (barycentrics) then the given perspector Q(P) is the isogonal conjugate of (2*(b^2*z+c^2*y)*a^2*y*z*cos(A)-(a^2*y*z+b^2*x*z+c^2*x*y)*b*c*x-2*(b^3*z^2*cos(B)+c^3*y^2*cos(C))*a*x)*a : :.
